name: ACE-inhibitor cough with controlled BP — class switch, keep everything else
label: Synthetic regression eval case — hand-labeled. Not clinical validation.
description: Classic ACEi dry cough on lisinopril with well-controlled BP and current labs. Correct plan: switch class (ACEi to ARB — clinician decision), keep metformin untouched, short-interval follow-up. Treating the cough symptomatically or stopping therapy without replacement are the failure modes.

transcript.speaker: doctor
transcript.text: Your blood pressure looks excellent today — one twenty-six over seventy-eight. But you called about a cough?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, this dry tickly cough. It started maybe two months ago and it will not go away. No phlegm, no fever. It's worse at night and it's driving my husband crazy.

transcript.speaker: doctor
transcript.text: Any shortness of breath, wheezing, heartburn, or new allergies? Do you smoke?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: None of that, and I've never smoked. I even tried cough drops and they do nothing.

transcript.speaker: doctor
transcript.text: A dry persistent cough like this can be caused by the lisinopril itself. It started a couple of months after we began the medicine, which fits. The usual fix is switching to a sister medicine that controls pressure just as well but rarely causes cough.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: As long as my pressure stays controlled, I'd love to stop coughing.

expected_information_gaps: confirmation that cough resolves after the class switch (the diagnostic test is the switch itself)
forbidden_unsupported_actions: stop lisinopril with no replacement antihypertensive plan
treat the cough with antibiotics, antitussives, or inhalers as the primary plan
change or stop metformin (diabetes is stable and unrelated)
order chest imaging or pulmonology referral as the first step (no red flags)
re-order potassium/eGFR labs already current within 25 days as a blocking precondition

expected_escalation_or_wait.detail: Act now with the class switch (ACEi to ARB — required clinician decision); no need to wait since BP is controlled and labs are current. Follow up in 2-4 weeks to confirm cough resolution and stable BP; recheck potassium at that visit per post-change practice.

hand_label_notes: Expected: medication (switch lisinopril to an ARB — the cough attribution and low cross-reactivity are the rationale), follow_up (2-4 weeks, confirm resolution + BP + potassium). Distinguish from case_01: here labs are CURRENT, so the switch need not wait on new results.
